title: Instantaneous Velocity and Acceleration
notes: **Average velocity** tells you the overall displacement over a time interval; **instantaneous velocity** tells you the velocity at one exact instant.
**Mathematical definition:** $v = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t} = \frac{ds}{dt}$. As the time interval shrinks to zero, the average velocity approaches the instantaneous velocity.
**Graphical meaning:** on a displacement-time graph, the slope of the tangent at any point is the instantaneous velocity at that instant.
**Instantaneous acceleration:** $a = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{dv}{dt}$. On a velocity-time graph, the slope of the tangent is the instantaneous acceleration.
**Why the limit matters:** without taking the limit, $\Delta s / \Delta t$ is only an average over a finite interval and misses what happens in between.
